events.text: I'll identify all studies/reports cited in the draft and search for the most recent updates simultaneously.
Now let me search for the State of CDR 2026 report and check whether the "2 GtCO2/yr" figure the draft uses from [4] has been updated, and also check the IPCC AR7 status.

I now have sufficient information to produce the JSON. Let me compile the findings carefully, comparing each figure the draft uses against the latest available data.

**Key figure comparisons:**

- **[4] Lück et al. (2024)** — The draft cites "current CDR approximates 2 GtCO2 per year, or about 3% of current global net greenhouse gas emissions." This figure originates from the Lamb et al. (2024) CDR gap paper [3], not [4]. The State of CDR 3rd Edition (June 2026) now reports **2.2 GtCO2/year = ~5% of gross CO2 emissions**. The draft's "2 GtCO2" and "3%" are both stale.
- **[3] Lamb et al. (2024)** — Published May 2024, Nature Climate Change 14(6):644–651. The draft's description of the CDR gap paper is consistent with the published version. However, the "2 GtCO2/yr" figure the draft attributes to [4] actually comes from [3]'s preprint/published version, which itself has been superseded by the SoCDR 3rd edition (2.2 GtCO2/yr).
- **[6] Fuss et al. (2018)** — The 2050 potential ranges (afforestation 0.5–3.6, BECCS 0.5–5, biochar 0.5–2, enhanced weathering 2–4, DACCS 0.5–5, soil carbon up to 5 GtCO2/yr) and the net zero CO2 timing (2046–2056) are from this 2018 paper. The SoCDR 3rd edition (2026) and IPCC AR6 (2022) both provide updated figures. The IPCC AR6 WGIII gives DACCS potential as 5–40 GtCO2/yr (much wider), and the SoCDR 3rd edition gives a mid-century central range of 7–9 GtCO2/yr total CDR needed. The 2018 Fuss figures are substantially superseded.
- **[1] IPCC AR6 WGIII (2022)** — Still the current IPCC assessment; AR7 is in draft (first order draft of WGIII circulated November 2026 per search result 62-6, but not yet published). AR6 remains the authoritative published IPCC source.
- **[5] National Academies (2019)** — The draft states it could not hold this source and draws nothing from it. No update needed.
- **[2] IPCC AR5 Synthesis (2023)** — The draft states it could not hold this source and draws nothing from it.

I could not open the full text of the paper, only the abstract, the preprint excerpt, the authors' policy brief and secondary reports. I found nothing that contradicts any of the six sentences. Sentences 1 and 5 match the abstract and the authors' statement that CDR is not a replacement for mitigation. Sentence 6 is a reasonable reading of the paper's caution about whether proposals become firm policy. All three objections are minor, and I would not ask for a correction on any of them.

I did not object to the net-zero window of 2046–2056, the 5–15 GtCO2/yr figure, or the 10–100 year saturation time. The review states all of these. I also did not object to the sentence on the penalty from compensating excess emissions with later removals. The review says the cooling from net negative emissions "may only offset part of the warming from earlier positive emissions."

The objection quotes: "the most ambitious proposals do come close to levels in a low-energy-demand scenario where CDR requirements are minimized" and the brief's reading that the CDR gap would be closed if countries pledge more ambitious emissions reductions. The held text has no such passage. It contains only a similar abstract sentence ("However, the most ambitious proposals for CDR are close to levels in a low-energy demand scenario with the most-limited CDR scaling and aggressive near-term emissions reductions."), which lacks the quoted wording and the authors' reading about closing the gap.

The held text only lists the brief as associated content (title and author names) and does not include its text. The closest passage is the abstract sentence 'However, the most ambitious proposals for CDR are close to levels in a low-energy demand scenario with the most-limited CDR scaling and aggressive near-term emissions reductions.', which does not contain the quoted wording or the claim about closing the gap."}

The held text contains the sentence, but without the surrounding quote marks and "(Abstract)" label. The exact passage as held is below.

{"source_says": "It is unlikely that a single NET will be able to sustainably meet the rates of carbon uptake described in integrated assessment pathways consistent with 1.5 °C of global warming.", "locator": "Abstract (opening sentence of the held text)", "could_not_find": ""}

Looking at the objection, the claim is that the page omits the companion clause about researching NETs. But checking the "already_on_the_page" list, I can see the full passage is already there:

"The direct policy implications of this NETs review are thus that, given the assessed uncertainties, strategies should aim at limiting warming to below 2 °C with the least possible assumed dependence on NETs. Simultaneously, NETs should be further researched, but until they are demonstrably available at the global scale there should be no delay in a global peak and decline of CO 2 emissions. Whether global temperature can be limited to 1.5 °C as part of the Paris Agreements long-term temperature goal will depend on the pace of technological learning and would require positive surprises compared to the current state of knowledge. If NETs become available at scale over the course of the next 50 years, they will still play a fundamental role in the context of 1.5 °C by enabling to revert global mean temperature rise from possibly higher peak levels."

The objected omission is already present on the page. There is no omitted finding to quote.
